findings: The registered source is the 85-page arXiv:2110.04924v4 PDF, stamped 16 May 2023, by Jelena Bradic, Weijie Ji and Yuqian Zhang. Its title and SHA-256 match the pinned original audit. This review does not substitute the journal typesetting for the registered preprint.

All 25 main-document pages were searched for actual theorem headings. Eleven environments occur: Theorem 1 on page 3; 2 on page 10; 3 and 4 on page 11; 5 on page 12; 6 on page 13; 7 on page 14; 8 on page 15; 9 and 10 on page 16; and 11 on page 18. Theorem 4 continues onto page 12 and its full continuation is preserved. The discussion, acknowledgment and supplement notice end on page 23; references occupy pages 24-25. The supplement title on page 26 establishes the boundary. No supplementary result or definition was used.

All eleven original statements were visually compared with fresh PDF renders. Theorem 1 retains its either/or correctness condition, Assumption 1, pointwise conditional expectation and printed grammatical wording. Theorems 6 and 7 retain their descriptive parentheticals in the statement body because the PDF places them after the numbered headings.

Theorem 2 retains the source mismatch between s2 in the rate and s2-prime in its definition, including its nested-model indicator despite the S-DRL setting. Theorem 3 uses two product-sparsity terms; Theorem 5 uses three. Theorems 4-5 explicitly replace the first-time DR working model and slope by their nested counterparts. Neither this replacement nor additional tuning-rate choices are inserted into other theorem statements.

Theorem 8 retains the strict imputation-error event, strict eigenvalue inequality, sample-size condition, both alternatives in the finite-sample bound, exact exponential probability denominator, and the complete asymptotic conclusion. Its original observations are i.i.d.; its imputed responses and errors need not be mutually independent or independent of covariates. This generic regression theorem has no causal-model dependencies.

Theorems 9 and 10 retain the signed r-th prediction powers without absolute values. All three Theorem 9 rate branches and their distinct model-correctness conditions are preserved. Theorem 10 imports the rate expression from 9(c), not all of that branch’s hypotheses. Its literal Assumptions 1-3 reference lacks the explicit nested-model substitution present in Theorems 4-5; the resulting ambiguity and DR-scale dependency remain visible.

All 37 interface records, original statements, source headings, source keywords, naming contexts and highlight selectors were checked. True propensity definitions, causal assumptions, general working functions, logistic and linear projections, DR and nested first-time projections, fitted estimators, and general imputed Lasso remain distinct. No synthesized definition replaces a source passage. All saved census content remains unchanged.

Both full algorithms on pages 6-7 were checked. S-DRL uses outer cross-fitting and two inner halves, exchanges the halves and averages the two first-time slopes. DTL uses the nested fitted second-time response and no DR inner imputation. Both retain the printed score formula, fold-specific contrasts and empirical variance estimates. Equation (2.12) retains its path-subscripted delta_c despite the unsubscripted argument binder; fold divisibility and unspecified K growth remain source notes.

Assumptions 1-6 and all fourteen auxiliary passages were reviewed. True overlap, working-model overlap, and fitted-model overlap with outer probability tending to one are distinguished. Assumption 5 borrows only the residual definitions from Assumption 2 and uses general working functions, normalized q-th moments and conditional second-moment bounds; it does not import the parametric sub-Gaussian hypothesis. Fresh-covariate expectation is distinguished from training-sample randomness.

The multi-stage model on page 17 and Theorem 11 on page 18 were checked independently of the two-stage Lasso setup. Histories, stage-specific propensities, terminal outcome and empty initial histories resolve the representation. The overlap formula’s lower-case covariate argument, terminal-coordinate notation, and absence of a printed lower bound on t are preserved; the following discussion supports t=0. Proposition 1 is excluded from the theorem inventory and is not a dependency of Theorem 11.

All 80 direct uses and recursive dependency reasons were reviewed, yielding 158 related-theorem connections. Distinct local NR application records preserve the explicit substitutions in Theorems 4-5. The general DR results do not acquire logistic/linear working-model assumptions. Theorem 9 requires its fitted nuisance slope and averaging instruction rather than the entire DTE algorithm. No proof-only connection or supplementary claim was added.

The source-convention notes preserve conditional-expectation version issues, argmin totality, possible zero scales and moment denominators, unquantified contrast-path uniformity, and the Orlicz gauge domain at zero. These are limitations of the printed definitions; the census does not silently repair them or certify proofs.

The previous scripts depended on source-provenance paths and temporary source images. They were archived under review-history/before-local-source-rebuild/scripts. The current inventory writer verifies the fixed registered PDF, and all content writers run through main entry points. The paper-specific rebuild regenerated six JSON artifacts byte for byte in an empty directory. Separate validator processes accept the inventory and final census; review evidence is saved independently of the rebuild.
